conviction_note: A slight negative lean, p_up 45 on an abs move of 5.5 (the 7.28 implied move shaded toward the name's 2.27 median, then pushed back up because a Q4 guide is issued every quarter). The negatives are Werner's 10-19 preannouncement, which put $0.18/sh of fuel, driver-pay and insurance headwind on Q2, and diesel rising $1.95 through Q3 after it fell $0.97 through Q2: KNX's own Q2 statement shows net fuel at +$24.0M against -$13.8M a year earlier, roughly $0.17/sh of the Q2 beat. The positive is JBHT's 10-15 print, with truckload pricing up 29% a load, which points to a strong Q4 rate guide. The findings sum to -1.1 and the scaled number is -0.55. The two are close because the sell-off from 76 to 63.5 and the -2.5% on the Werner day have already priced part of the cost story.
bar: Q3 adj EPS guide $0.71-0.77 (company, Q2 release 2026-07-22, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1492691/000149269126000055/exhibit99106302026.htm). findings.finding: Werner (direct asset-truckload peer) preannounced Q3 on 2026-10-19: adj EPS about $0.15-0.16, GAAP $0.10-0.11, revenue $946-951M, with about $0.18/sh of headwind against Q2 from rising fuel prices, driver recruitment and retention spending, and a late-quarter insurance reserve adjustment for prior claims. Those are the same three cost lines that carry KNX's truckload segment (KNX Q2 insurance and claims already +17.5% YoY to $100.2M). The KNX street figure of 0.76 sits at the top of its 0.71-0.77 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KNX fell -2.5% (64.81 to 63.21) on 10-19, the Werner day; WERN fell -7.9% (32.81 to 30.22). On its own Q2 print (a big beat, Q3 guided above) KNX fell -4.88%, so cost-quality questions have been sold even on beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: KNX lost 2.5% that day. If the market had fully carried a peer-wide cost hit into KNX, the 0.76 estimate (top of guide) would have come down. It still reads 0.76 on finviz, and the options are not skewed to the downside (-0.26).
findings.independence: Partly shares a mechanism with the diesel finding (fuel is one of Werner's three items), so the two are sized smaller rather than merged. Different document: EIA diesel series https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_NUS_DPG&f=W. Driver pay and insurance are not corroborated by a second document.

findings.finding: Diesel rose through Q3 after falling through Q2, which reverses a fuel tailwind that carried much of KNX's Q2 beat. EIA retail diesel went from $5.64 (04-06) to $4.67 (06-29) in Q2, then from $4.58 (07-06) to $6.53 (09-21) in Q3. KNX's Q2 statement shows fuel surcharge revenue of $331.3M against fuel expense of $307.4M, a net +$24.0M against -$13.8M in Q2 2025. That +$37.8M swing is roughly $0.17/sh after tax on 163.3M shares, set against a $47M YoY gain in adjusted operating income. A rising price means surcharge lag in truckload. The Q3 guide was given on 07-22, with diesel at $5.13 and rising, so part of this may already be inside it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No KNX release isolates fuel as the swing line. Q2 2026, which carried the favourable lag, beat ($0.63 against about $0.51) and the stock fell -4.88% anyway.
findings.why_not_priced: The net-fuel arithmetic sits in the income statement, not in the headline beat, and the 0.76 street figure at the top of the guide suggests the Q2 run rate was extrapolated. Offset: LTL surcharges are percentage-based and rise with diesel (ODFL Q3-to-date revenue/cwt +11.3% including fuel against +4.8% excluding), so the net is smaller than the truckload lag alone. Sized net of that; a print inside the 0.71-0.77 guide is something the company told the market to expect.
findings.independence: EIA weekly diesel series https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_NUS_DPG&f=W (independent price data). Werner names rising fuel as a Q3 headwind (shared with the Werner finding). The fuel lines are this filer's own primary document; the Q3 lag effect is my inference.

findings.finding: J.B. Hunt's Q3 (10-15) confirms truckload pricing tightened sharply in Q3: JBT revenue per load +29% excluding fuel on loads +4%, ICS revenue per load +29%, intermodal loads +8% with revenue/load +2% excluding fuel. JBT and ICS margins were squeezed by higher third-party capacity costs. Read through, this supports KNX truckload rate per mile (guide: truckload revenue excluding fuel up mid-single digits, OR 650-750 bp better) and a strong Q4 rate guide. It is a negative for KNX Logistics, whose gross margin was already 15.4% (-350 bp YoY).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KNX rose +3.3% (63.21 to 65.28) on 10-15 as JBHT fell -2.8%. KNX's last strong rate-acceleration message (the Q2 call, June rates up high-single digits) was followed by -4.88%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through the +3.3% on 10-15, which then reversed (65.28 to 63.25 by 10-20). Asset truckload rates are a guidance and Q4 line, and the Q4 guide is not public until tonight. If the rate tailwind were fully priced, KNX would not sit 23% below its high with sell-side targets at $86.6. Logistics is about 7% of KNX revenue, so the third-party cost squeeze is a small net-off.
findings.independence: KNX's own Q2 release: later bids reflected tighter conditions and June rate growth accelerated (same filer, different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1492691/000149269126000055/exhibit99106302026.htm).

findings.finding: Old Dominion's August update (09-03): LTL revenue/day +12.4%, tons/day -0.9%, shipments/day -2.4%, Q3-to-date revenue/cwt excluding fuel +4.8%, demand described as fairly stable. This is consistent with KNX's LTL guide (revenue excluding fuel up low-single digits, adj OR in the low 90s) and with fuel surcharges lifting LTL revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated in KNX history. Q2 LTL adj OR 92.1% (100 bp better) sat inside a print that fell -4.88%.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and public for seven weeks; it mostly confirms the in-guide case. Filed as a proxy for KNX's LTL segment, about 19% of revenue excluding fuel.
findings.independence: none (single peer series; KNX LTL is AAA Cooper/DHE, a regional network that differs from ODFL's)

baseline_tension: The lean is mildly negative, which fits the 20-day decline and the call-heavy, balanced-skew options only loosely. The skew says nothing directional, and the stock has already absorbed part of the cost story (76 down to 63.5, -2.5% on the Werner day), so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the diesel finding cut from -1.2 to -0.9, because a print near the 0.71-0.77 midpoint is something the company guided to, even though it misses the 0.76 street figure.
Rule 1 (beats sold, Q2 -4.88% on a beat with a raise): the JBHT pricing / Q4-guide finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7.
Rule 5 / 'what has worked' (a peer's print after the company last spoke): left the Werner finding at -1.0 rather than cutting it as a proxy.
Rule 7: short interest checked (8.37%, 3.77 days), not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk; skew balanced.
Pessimism artefact: p_up kept at 45, not moved lower. The sum is unchanged at -1.1 because the two cuts net against each other; no lesson was applied twice.
